title: Who merges pull requests that hold only decision records or documentation?
context: Picks made in the hub land on a standing docs/decisions branch with one rolling pull request (decision 35), and every merge has needed Matt's word (decisions 7 and 22). On 2026-11-12 that meant three separate 'merge' replies for records-only pull requests. Matt said that having to say merge each time is the part that bothers him, and that records-only and documentation-only merges are fine without his approval in most of his repos.

options.name: Keep as is
options.summary: One rolling records pull request; Matt says merge each time.
pros: No change to the rule that every merge is Matt's
cons: A merge reply for every pick, with nothing in it for Matt to review

options.name: Records ride with the build
options.summary: The record goes into the pull request of the work that builds it.
cons: Picks that lead to no code have no home
The record reaches main later than the pick
options.effort: A change to how the hub lands picks

options.name: The orchestrator merges records-only and documentation-only pull requests
options.summary: When a pull request changes nothing but decision records and documentation, the orchestrator merges it without asking and tells Matt in one line. Every other merge stays Matt's. Each person sets this per repo; it is Matt's rule for this repo and most of his others.
pros: Removes the merge reply that carries no real review
Code merges, pushes to main, force pushes and deletions stay with Matt
Still one line in the thread for each merge, so nothing happens unseen
cons: Documentation in a public repo can still leak something private, so the orchestrator must check what the pull request contains before merging
Needs a clear line for what counts as documentation
options.effort: A rule for the orchestrator now; a per-repo setting in the hub later if wanted

recommendation: Matt's own rule. The line used: a pull request counts as records-only or documentation-only when every changed file is under .decisions/ or is a Markdown document (README, INSTALL, guides, notes) or a picture those documents show. Anything that runs or is published as a product (code, scripts, settings, package files, the public web page in site/) is not documentation for this rule. Before merging, the orchestrator checks the file list, checks it merges cleanly, and in a public repo checks nothing private is in it; when in doubt it asks.
reason: Having to say merge each time is what bothers me. In general, documentation-only PRs and merges are fine with me. In most of my repos, I'm fine with the orchestrator merging records-only / documentation without my approval.

settles.value: the orchestrator may merge pull requests that change only decision records and documentation (Markdown and its pictures), reporting each in one line; set per repo by the human; all other merges stay with the human (see agent git push authority)
